bug_description.normalized: The saved 27-byte witness `rule r{strings:$=/.{369}? /` reaches YARA's regexp string parser with token `.{369}? `, which the regexp grammar turns into a concat AST whose first child is a non-greedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` with `start = end = 369` and whose second child is a literal space. In vulnerable commit `459d5a2bae0f4c9a2921be0d21fe920258cb5d6d`, `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point` accepts that first child as a chaining point because it checks only `!child->greedy`, `child->type == RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY`, and the `YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD` comparison; it does not require both `child->prev_sibling` and `child->next_sibling`. The first split allocates a non-null `remainder_re_ast`, builds a `concat` node with `children_head` still pointing at that first child and `children_tail = NULL`, assigns `(*remainder_re_ast)->root_node = concat`, and then frees the child with `yr_re_node_destroy(child)`. `yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration` sees that non-null `remainder_re_ast` and immediately calls `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point` again on the corrupted AST. The second traversal reloads the freed node from `remainder_re_ast->root_node->children_head` and crashes on the first `child->greedy` read, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-use-after-free READ at `libyara/re.c:480`. Commit `8eeed3ef5e2bbd5b927bf1b72879c1fa9ab979cb` fixes the bug by requiring both siblings before splitting.

source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact rule text `rule r{strings:$=/.{369}? /`. YARA's rule lexer reduces the `_REGEXP_` token to `str->c_string = ".{369}? "`, and line 544 passes that exact regex body into the regexp parser.

root_cause.code: if (!child->greedy && child->type == RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY && (child->start > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD || child->end > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD))
root_cause.description: The split predicate accepts a large ungreedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` even when it is the first or last concat child. The vulnerable guard omits the `child->prev_sibling != NULL && child->next_sibling != NULL` precondition added by the fix, so a boundary gap node reaches the split logic and leaves stale AST references behind.
root_cause.note: For the witness regex `.{369}? `, the candidate gap node is the first concat child, so `child->prev_sibling == NULL` and only the trailing literal space is to its right. The fix commit adds both sibling checks to this exact guard before any AST rewiring happens.

tainted_value_origin.description: AddressSanitizer allocation origin for the heap `RE_NODE` later freed in the first split and reread in the second split. `re_yyparse` reaches this allocator when the witness token `.{369}?` is reduced to a `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY`.

parser_admitted.description: The YARA rule parser accepts the witness far enough to reduce a regexp string declaration and invoke `yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration`; the crash happens during this reduction before the incomplete rule text would be rejected later.

coarse_trace.summary: The rule parser hands the attacker-controlled regexp token `.{369}? ` to YARA's regexp parser so it can build a regexp AST for the string declaration.
The regexp grammar builds a concat AST whose first child is a non-greedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` for `.{369}?` and whose second child is the trailing literal space.

The first split treats that boundary gap node as a valid chaining point, allocates a remainder AST, installs a concat root whose head still aliases the gap node, rewires the original AST past that node, and then frees the gap node.

Because the first split returned a non-null `remainder_re_ast`, the chaining loop calls `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point` again on that corrupted AST, and the second traversal reads the freed node at `child->greedy`.

fine_trace.note: This is the first project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled regexp token extracted from the rule text. For the saved witness, `str->c_string` is `.{369}? `, and this call materializes the AST later processed by the chaining splitter.

Parsing `.{369}?` allocates the heap `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` that later becomes stale, then stores the witness-controlled range bounds `start = end = 369` and marks the node non-greedy. AddressSanitizer's allocation stack points to `yr_re_node_create` reached from this reduction.

The witness regexp is a concatenation of the leading range-any node and a trailing literal space. The first append makes the gap node the concat `children_head`; the second append links the literal as `next_sibling`, leaving the gap node with `prev_sibling == NULL` and `next_sibling != NULL`.

fine_trace.code: if (!child->greedy && child->type == RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY && (child->start > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD || child->end > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD))
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The first split sees that the concat head is a non-greedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` with `start = end = 369`, which is above `YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD` 200, and enters the split logic. The guard never checks that the candidate gap has both a left and right sibling, so it accepts the witness's first-child gap node as a chaining point.

The first split allocates a fresh `RE_AST` for the remainder path and stores it through `*remainder_re_ast`. `yr_re_ast_create` initializes that object with `root_node = NULL`, so `remainder_re_ast` is now non-null before any node is attached to it.

A new concat node is prepared for the remainder AST. Because the witness gap node is the first concat child, `child->prev_sibling` is `NULL`, so `concat->children_head = child` and `concat->children_tail = NULL`, while the original AST is rewired to start at the trailing literal space.

The non-null `*remainder_re_ast` from step 5 now receives `concat` as its root and inherits the AST flags. Because step 6 left `concat->children_head = child`, the returned remainder AST is now a live alias to the soon-to-be-freed gap node.

The first split frees the `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` object allocated for `.{369}?`. After this call the heap object is invalid, but step 7 already installed a remainder AST whose root still reaches that same node through `children_head`. AddressSanitizer's free stack points to this exact call.

Because step 7 returned `remainder_re_ast != NULL`, the chaining loop executes and passes that remainder AST back into `yr_re_ast_split_at_chaining_point` after destroying the prior `re_ast`. This is the stale-use path that reaches the second traversal.

fine_trace.code: if (!child->greedy && child->type == RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY && (child->start > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD || child->end > YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD))
fine_trace.note: Sink. In the second split call, `child` is reloaded from `remainder_re_ast->root_node->children_head`, which still points to the freed range node from step 8 because step 7 made `concat` the remainder AST root. Evaluating `child->greedy` triggers the saved 4-byte heap-use-after-free read at `libyara/re.c:480`.

poc.trigger: Feed the saved rule text to `rules_fuzzer`; during regexp string declaration reduction, YARA parses `/.{369}? /`, performs one split that allocates `remainder_re_ast` and installs a concat root for it, and then crashes when the chaining loop resubmits that corrupted remainder AST to the splitter.

format.name: YARA rule source text
format.contract: A textual YARA rule that reaches `yr_parser_reduce_string_declaration` with regexp token `.{369}? `, so the regexp AST is a concat whose first child is an ungreedy `RE_NODE_RANGE_ANY` with `start = end = 369` (> `YR_STRING_CHAINING_THRESHOLD` 200) and whose second child is the trailing literal space. That exact boundary split allocates `remainder_re_ast`, sets `(*remainder_re_ast)->root_node = concat`, and leaves `concat->children_head` pointing at the freed gap node.
